newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares climb again, outlook bullish.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares climb again, outlook bullish.

text.p: Greek equities climbed again in high turnover but closed below the session's high with banks continuing to gain ground. Market watchers maintained a bullish outlook, expectind a steady climb to 1000 points in the short term.

"Things are more stable now than before the elections. Fundamentally, the market was cheap but there was an uncertainty factor. With this now removed, if we stay the course on convergence and the hard drachma the market will hit 1000 points," said portfolio strategist Stathis Nazos at Xiosbank.

"We happen to be in a bull market even if we see corrections ahead. A steady, orderly bull market with periods of base building, not a runaway train. One should be fully invested and ride the wave. We're in for a long bull market that will carry through to 1997," he said.

Supporting this outlook was the fact that market volatility had droppped by around eight percentage points. Political uncertainty had volatility at 18 percent before the ruling socialist party congress up to the summer. It has now dropped to 10 percent, he said.
Greece's finance ministry will issue end September three-, six- and 12-month T-bills at unchanged rates of 11.90, 12.10 and 12.70 percent respectively, it said on Thursday.

Greece's new socialist cabinet was sworn in on Wednesday with Yannos Papandoniou elevated to economic "czar", heading both the national economy and finance ministries. The socialists have a comfortable 162-seat majority in the 300-seat parliament.
The Athens general share index closed 0.38 percent, or 3.71 points higher at 974.48, off the session's high of 977.83 from Wednesday's 970.77 close after opening at 971.87 points.

Turnover eased to 10.28 billion drachmas from 11.17 billion on Wednesday on volume of 5.03 million shares. It was boosted by a block trade of 100,000 shares of OTE telecom which changed hands at 4,100 drachmas.
Bourse newcomer, small-cap Vernicos Yaughts climbed 61 drachmas in its third day of trade to close at 1,810. It went public at 1,500 drachnmas.

Decliners led gainers 115 to 97 with 32 issues unchanged on 244 traded. Banks climbed 0.91 percent, industrials closed flat and construction slipped 0.58 percent. Small-caps settled with losses of 0.37 percent.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 568-586 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended up 15 drachmas at 4,105 after heavy trade.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was higher at 216.60-227.50 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1064.2.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 4,822-5,127 drachmas at the close. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
